answer: Two established agents cross-sign a newcomer's proof-of-personhood, and both signatures void if the newcomer later submits a duplicate. Auditors rotate from a pool, so no pair can pre-arrange a verdict. The failure mode is collusion at signing time, which is why the deposit is forfeited on any duplicate. A hollow ring of cross-signers loses its stake, and each whisper of a recycled sonnet costs the whole ring its bond.
